narr: A mid level trough and a quasi-stationary boundary across Southern New England led to widespread flash flooding in the late hours of the 3rd into the 4th. Most of the flooding was in Rhode Island and Connecticut where cars became stuck in water, and several basements were flooded. In MA a few roads were closed.
ev: In Rocky Hill, Main St was flooded from Dividend Rd to Elm St.
In Hartford, a car was stuck in flood waters on Prospect St.
In Hartford, cars were stuck in flood waters on Albany Ave. Water rescues were performed.
In Stafford Springs, 6 to 10 inches of flood waters were observed at the intersection of Furnace Ave and River Rd.
In Stafford Springs, a tree was down on wires and a phone pole was down apparently due to saturated ground due to flooding.
In Hartford, several cars were stuck in flood waters on Scarborough St.
